items.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023
items.q: a good wedding like Oscar Peterson played for Prince Charles’ and Diana’s wedding

ctx.x: I’m always surprised when I learn about musicians that I listened to and read about when — growing up, and in some cases I got to meet them and to find out that they would play gigs that I would never imagine. That they would play weddings, you know, because everybody’s got to make a buck.

Right. And then too, I’m going to tell you all this truth, man — it’s nothing wrong with playing a wedding. I played a wedding in 2012 with the same band I had in Dizzy’s Coca Cola, because the guy was a friend of mine and he was a fan of mine and he loved jazz you know, and he wanted a real jazz group at his daughter’s wedding. You know? So we played it you know? But what’s wrong with playing a miscellaneous wedding for miscellaneous people for miscellaneous money on a miscellaneous circumstance. But a good…
I played for a funeral, I played for a birthday party, but the real deal, not no jive, this poverty-stricken, you know, and academically deplete you know, depleted or whatever you know.
